clue.text: Fateful rioting traps new rich

indicators.note: traps means one piece closes round another, holding it inside
a rioting crowd is in disorder, so the letters of the word before are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A fatal riot catches out the newly wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rioting' rearranges FATEFUL into AFFLUET, and 'traps' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone with plenty of money; they are synonyms.

clue.text: MD, for example, identifying crisis

definitions.meaning: a managing director is the boss of a firm, the person in charge
a crisis point, as in 'things came to a ...'

explanation.walkthrough: MD suggests a doctor first; here it is a managing director. 'identifying' just links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A managing director is the chief of a company, and a matter that 'comes to a head' reaches its decisive point.

clue.text: User of commercial reference work

parts.note: a commercial on TV or radio is an advert, shortened to ad
dict. is the usual abbreviation for dictionary, a reference work

explanation.surface: Someone who uses an advertiser's guidebook.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug user is someone dependent on a substance, an addict.

clue.text: Fair rent? Play for time, lots of time

parts.note: to stall is to delay deliberately, playing for time
an age is a very long time, as in 'it took ages'

explanation.surface: A tenant at a reasonable rent stalls for ages before paying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair rent' reads as a reasonable rent; here 'fair' is a market or fair, and the rent is the charge for a stall there.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the fee paid for the right to set up a stall at a market or fair.

clue.text: Watch, perhaps, the enemy defender

parts.note: from the saying 'time is the enemy'
a goalkeeper or wicket-keeper defends the goal or stumps

explanation.surface: A guard watches out for the foe while defending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time is the enemy' is a common saying, so 'the enemy' gives TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is one example of a device that records the hours.

clue.text: Officer turned up in a revolutionary hat

indicators.note: in places the turned officer inside the revolutionary

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary in crosswords

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: COL is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer

explanation.surface: An officer appears in a rebel's headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' reads the officer from bottom to top; Che Guevara is the stock revolutionary, and 'a' belongs to him.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloche is a close-fitting bell-shaped women's hat popular in the 1920s.

clue.text: Criminal objective is concealed in advance

indicators.note: being concealed in something means being placed inside it

parts.note: an advance is an offer or proposal, as in making advances
an end is an aim or objective, as in 'to that end'

explanation.surface: A villain's aim is hidden before the act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in advance' reads as 'beforehand'; here 'advance' is an offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal is a lawbreaker, someone who commits an offence.

clue.text: Salad plant right with a particular variety of food

parts.note: a dish is a specific kind of prepared food

explanation.surface: A vegetable goes nicely with a certain meal.
explanation.definitionFit: This red root vegetable is commonly eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Bird sounds from teal, primarily, on brooklets

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the opening letter of teal

parts.note: rills are small streams or brooklets

explanation.surface: Ducks calling as they sit on little streams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' picks T, the first letter of 'teal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Songbirds warble with rapid quivering notes, which are called trills.

clue.text: Some erotic ladies appearing thus in striptease, initially

indicators.note: some here means only part of the words that follow, so the answer is found inside them

explanation.surface: Risqué dancers start off dressed before they strip.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'eroti-C LAD-ies'. A striptease starts with the performer dressed, hence 'initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clad means dressed, which is how a stripper begins the act.

clue.text: Pardon the extravagance

definitions.meaning: in the medieval church a papal remission of punishment for sin
a luxury allowed to oneself, a treat

explanation.walkthrough: 'the' just links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval church sold remissions of sin by this name, and the word also means a treat or self-gratification.

clue.text: Tree planted in favourite border of wood

indicators.note: planted in means set inside, as a tree is put in the ground

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
the elm is a common tree

explanation.surface: A tree is planted in a favourite spot at the edge of a wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border of wood' suggests a forest edge; here it is a wooden strip above a window.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelmet is a narrow board fitted above a window to hide the curtain fixings.

clue.text: Very little help needed to see part of 5

parts.note: minute means tiny
a hand is help, as in 'give me a hand'

explanation.surface: Only a little assistance is needed to see something.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 refers to the answer at 5 down, a watch; this is one of its pointers. 'needed to see' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch face has two pointers, the longer one marking minutes.

clue.text: Those who rocket to fame among stars

definitions.text: Those who rocket to fame among stars

parts.words: Those who rocket to fame among stars
parts.note: reads as celebrities shooting to stardom, but describes astronauts literally rocketed up among the stars

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about sudden celebrity; the real sense is rocket travel to space.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronauts are carried by rocket into outer space among the stars.

clue.text: Preserves the Spanish element in show

parts.note: to tin food is to preserve it in cans
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Jam and Spanish flavour feature in a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserves' reads as jam, a noun; here it is a verb, cans.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinsel is a glittering decoration, the showy part of a display.

clue.text: Blighted tiny tree in dead state

indicators.note: a blighted plant is damaged and spoilt, signalling that the letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A small diseased tree is dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blighted' rearranges TINYTREE.
explanation.definitionFit: After death, in religious thought, one passes into everlasting time.

clue.text: Moderate's state of mind

definitions.meaning: a verb meaning to soften or tone down
a mood, as in 'in a good ...'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' looks like a noun for a centrist; it is a verb here, and the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To soften something is to tone it down, and one's mood can be called one's disposition or humour.

clue.text: Kicked, wound again?

definitions.meaning: a gun kicks when it jumps back after firing
coiled or wound up once more

explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' reads as injured; here it is the past of 'wind'.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm springs back on firing, and a rope wound a second time has been coiled again.

clue.text: Union reportedly dubbed "Amalgamated"

indicators.note: reportedly signals that what follows is how the words sound when spoken

parts.note: to dub someone is to knight them by tapping a sword on the shoulder

explanation.surface: A trade union is said to have been named 'Amalgamated'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' works on the sound: with U in front, 'knighted' said aloud is 'you-nighted', which is how the whole word is pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: Firms or bodies that have amalgamated have joined together as one.

clue.text: Starlet represented Northern woman of untidy appearance

indicators.note: re-presented, that is, presented again in a different form

explanation.surface: An actress played a scruffy northern woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges STARLET into SLATTER, then N is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A slattern is an old word for a slovenly, dirty woman.

clue.text: Drink served round a camp

indicators.note: round means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: lager is a drink served in pubs

explanation.surface: Beer handed out around the camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts LAGER around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A laager is a South African defensive camp ringed with wagons.

clue.text: Great poet in House, leading the people

indicators.note: leading means coming in front, so house goes before the people

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A grand poet in the Commons leads the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' suggests Parliament; here it is simply HO, the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: This Roman poet of the Odes is one of the great Latin writers.

clue.text: Flowering plant almost open

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: honesty is a flowering plant with papery silver seed pods

explanation.surface: A blooming plant is nearly in flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' removes the final Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open means being frank and truthful, without deceit.

clue.text: A night snow raged in American state

indicators.note: a raging storm is wild, signalling that the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A snowstorm raged at night in a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raged' rearranges ANIGHTSNOW.
explanation.definitionFit: This north-western US state lies on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Talk angrily about grouse or another bird

definitions.meaning: 'another' because grouse is a bird too

explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' is both a complaint, giving the sense of the first definition, and a bird, which is why the second says 'another bird'. 'or' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: To rant against something is to protest angrily, and the water rail is a wading bird.

clue.text: European capital invested in irrigation

indicators.note: invested in means held inside, so the answer is found within the next word

explanation.surface: A capital city's money is put into irrigation.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'ir-RIGA-tion'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital city of Latvia.

clue.text: Curdled milk, note, on the turn

indicators.note: on the turn means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note

explanation.surface: Milk has curdled; it is about to go off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the turn' is also said of milk going sour. A tenner is a British ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Rennet, from a calf's stomach, curdles milk; the word also names curds made that way.

clue.text: Sin and greed corrupted person making plans

indicators.note: something corrupted is twisted out of its true form, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Sin and greed corrupt a planner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupted' rearranges SINGREED; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A designer is one who draws up plans for a product or building.
